title: One Point Lesson - Manual Bypass (HV-6701) Operation (OPL-LV-6701-05)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-LV-6701-05 - Manual Bypass (HV-6701) Operation.

Equipment: LV-6701 (SEPARATOR LEVEL CONTROL VALVE), Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 6700 - LP SEPARATOR SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-6701 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-6701.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains manual bypass (hv-6701) operation for LV-6701 (SEPARATOR LEVEL CONTROL VALVE) in the LP SEPARATOR SYSTEM. The manual bypass lets operators keep the separator level safely while LV-6701 is isolated for maintenance. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Operating procedure & P&ID
- Tool 2: Radio / communication with panel
- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Notify the panel and take LIC-6701 to manual
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Crack open the bypass HV-6701 slowly
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Throttle HV-6701 to hold FA-6710 level using LT-6710
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Isolate LV-6701 (close block valves) for the work
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Reverse the steps and re-establish auto control afterwards
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: LV-6701 isolation for planned maintenance | Likely Cause: Planned - bypass used to hold level | Action: Lined up HV-6701 manual bypass, isolated LV-6701 safely
- Symptom: LV-6701 not responding to LIC-6701, level control lost | Likely Cause: Stem seized in PTFE packing (over-tightened + fines) | Action: Freed stem, renewed packing, lubricated, re-stroked and calibrated
- Symptom: Manual handwheel jack on LV-6701 seized | Likely Cause: Corrosion in handwheel thread | Action: Overhauled handwheel assembly, greased thread

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: The manual bypass lets operators keep the separator level safely while LV-6701 is isolated for maintenance.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-6701: e.g. LSHH-6710 trips at > 85 % - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-6701 before working on LV-6701.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
